sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯汀·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过 nytimes.com 进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: November 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Until recently, many American Jews believed that anti-Semitism was a European problem, one they had left behind.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，许多美国犹太人还认为反犹太主义是一个欧洲问题，一个他们早已抛在脑后的问题。

sentences.en: But the attack in Pittsburgh didn't come out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 但匹兹堡的袭击并非凭空而来。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月30日，星期二。

sentences.en: Jonathan, tell us what happened on May 18th, 2016.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，告诉我们2016年5月18日发生了什么。

sentences.en: On May 18th, 2016, in the middle of the presidential campaign, I read a column by a conservative Jewish
sentences.zh: 2016年5月18日，在总统竞选期间，我读了一篇由一位保守派犹太

sentences.en: writer named Robert Kagan and was called, This is How Fascism Comes to America.
sentences.zh: 作家罗伯特·卡根写的专栏文章，标题是《法西斯主义是如何来到美国的》。

sentences.en: And, you know, as I do a lot, I copied, pasted, put it on Twitter and sent it out into the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像我经常做的那样，我复制、粘贴，发到推特上，把它推向了世界。

sentences.en: And fairly quickly, I got a very strange reply from somebody named at Cybertrump.
sentences.zh: 很快，我就收到了一个叫 Cybertrump 的人发来的非常奇怪的回复。

sentences.en: And all it said was,
sentences.zh: 上面只写着：

sentences.en: Hello, Weissman.
sentences.zh: 你好，韦斯曼。

sentences.en: But Weissman, strangely enough, was in three parentheses, three open parentheses, three closed parentheses.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，韦斯曼这个名字被括在三层括号里，三个左括号，三个右括号。

sentences.en: And I had never seen that notation.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未见过这种符号。

sentences.en: So I sent something back.
sentences.zh: 所以我回了一条信息。

sentences.en: I said,
sentences.zh: 我说：

sentences.en: Care to explain?
sentences.zh: 能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: And then he sent me another note back saying, What ho, the vaunted Ashkenazi intelligence.
sentences.zh: 然后他回了我一条信息说：哟，这就是所谓的阿什肯纳兹犹太人的智慧吗？

sentences.en: It's a dog whistle, fool.
sentences.zh: 这是个狗哨，蠢货。

sentences.en: I was belling the cat for my fellow goyim.
sentences.zh: 我是在为我的外邦人同胞给猫挂铃铛呢。

sentences.en: And by belling the cat, this person literally meant I am putting a digital bell on Jonathan Weissman's
sentences.zh: 而所谓的“给猫挂铃铛”，这个人字面上的意思是，我正在给乔纳森·韦斯曼的

sentences.en: Twitter handle so that it will ring what exactly?
sentences.zh: 推特账号挂上一个数字铃铛，这样它就会响，响什么呢？

sentences.en: Jew.
sentences.zh: 犹太人。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: He had put those three parentheses around my name.
sentences.zh: 他在我的名字周围加上了那三个括号。

sentences.en: And unbeknownst to me, there was a piece of software.
sentences.zh: 而我当时并不知道，有一款软件存在。

sentences.en: It's actually called the coincidence indicator, blandly named, so Google wouldn't notice that it was sitting on the Google plugin website.
sentences.zh: 它实际上被称为“巧合指标”，名字起得很平淡，这样谷歌就不会注意到它正挂在谷歌插件网站上。

sentences.en: And anyone who plugged in the coincidence indicator could actually search for those three parentheses.
sentences.zh: 任何安装了“巧合指标”的人都可以搜索那三个括号。

sentences.en: So if a leader of the alt-right decides to tag you, to bell you with those three parentheses, then all of his followers who have downloaded the
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个另类右翼的领导人决定标记你，用那三个括号给你挂上铃铛，那么他所有下载了

sentences.en: coincidence indicator, then can swarm you.
sentences.zh: “巧合指标”的追随者就可以蜂拥而至攻击你。

sentences.en: Jonathan Weissman is deputy Washington editor of The Times.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·韦斯曼是《时报》华盛顿分社副主编。

sentences.en: You know, your notifications on Twitter start lighting up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的推特通知开始闪个不停。

sentences.en: And you're curious, like, what is this?
sentences.zh: 你会很好奇，这是什么？

sentences.en: How come I have 1,000 new notifications in the last two minutes?
sentences.zh: 为什么我在过去两分钟内收到了1000条新通知？

sentences.en: And you click on it, and you see my face photoshopped on a picture from World War II of a Jew kneeling by a Nazi.
sentences.zh: 当你点开它，你会看到我的脸被PS在一张二战照片上，照片里是一个犹太人跪在纳粹旁边。

sentences.en: Or my head photoshopped on a bunch of concentration camp victims shot in
sentences.zh: 或者我的头被PS在一堆在

sentences.en: Auschwitz.
sentences.zh: 奥斯威辛集中营被枪杀的受害者身上。

sentences.en: And then, of course, it begins to creep into your emails, your phone voicemails.
sentences.zh: 当然，这随后开始蔓延到你的电子邮件和语音留言中。

sentences.en: It doesn't just get contained on social media.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅局限于社交媒体。

sentences.en: So just from these three brackets being put on either side of your name, you are suddenly opened
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅因为名字两边被加上了这三个括号，你就突然暴露

sentences.en: up to this whole underworld of anti-Semitism that feels like a coordinated swarm, an attempt to kind of out of nowhere attack you.
sentences.zh: 在整个反犹太主义的地下世界中，这感觉就像一场协同的围攻，一种试图凭空攻击你的行为。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And several Jewish journalists were tagged around this time.
sentences.zh: 当时有几位犹太记者都被标记了。

sentences.en: I was not the only one.
sentences.zh: 我不是唯一一个。

sentences.en: But the Anti-Depamation League actually tabulated the attacks on Jewish journalists during the 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 但反诽谤联盟确实统计了2016年竞选期间针对犹太记者的攻击。

sentences.en: I did come in the top 10.
sentences.zh: 我确实排进了前十名。

sentences.en: I was number five, but by no means was I number one.
sentences.zh: 我是第五名，但绝不是第一名。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: And Jonathan, what do you remember thinking at the time when this started?
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，当这一切开始时，你记得当时在想什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I grew up in the South, in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我在南方长大，在亚特兰大。

sentences.en: I actually didn't experience a lot of anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 我其实并没有经历过很多反犹太主义。

sentences.en: I went to Sunday school.
sentences.zh: 我上过主日学校。

sentences.en: I also joked that my Sunday school was Holocaust studies because basically we learned the history of oppression of our people.
sentences.zh: 我还开玩笑说我的主日学校其实是犹太人大屠杀研究课，因为我们基本上学习的是我们民族受压迫的历史。

sentences.en: But it all seemed very, very distant.
sentences.zh: 但这一切看起来都非常、非常遥远。

sentences.en: You know, we learned all of these tropes about anti-Semitism, that the
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们学习了所有关于反犹太主义的陈词滥调，比如

sentences.en: Jew was both a radical leftist Marxist bomber and a rapacious banker, that Jews were both sniveling cowards and all powerful puppet masters.
sentences.zh: 犹太人既是激进的左翼马克思主义炸弹客，又是贪婪的银行家；犹太人既是卑躬屈膝的懦夫，又是全能的幕后操纵者。

sentences.en: The Jew could be anything to anybody just as long as it's bad.
sentences.zh: 只要是坏事，犹太人可以是任何人。

sentences.en: And all of that stuff that seemed, you know, pre-Nazi, maybe coming during the pogrom era of Russia.
sentences.zh: 所有这些东西看起来，你知道，像是纳粹之前的东西，也许是俄罗斯大屠杀时代传下来的。

sentences.en: But it was the past, right?
sentences.zh: 但这已经是过去式了，对吧？

sentences.en: The United States was the land of the free.
sentences.zh: 美国是自由之地。

sentences.en: This was a backward looking world that American Jews had left.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美国犹太人已经抛弃的、向后看的旧世界。

sentences.en: Germany, Russia.
sentences.zh: 德国、俄罗斯。

sentences.en: This was not America.
sentences.zh: 那不是美国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's this kind of distant thing that you're taught as kind of our collective past, but not something that's happening now, something that's been escaped.
sentences.zh: 这是一种遥远的事情，被当作我们共同的过去来教导，而不是现在正在发生的事情，是一种已经被逃离的东西。

sentences.en: You know, the remarkable thing is that growing up, I went to a synagogue called The Temple in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最引人注目的是，我小时候在亚特兰大的一家名为“圣殿”的犹太会堂做礼拜。

sentences.en: And only when I was researching the book that I wrote about all of this, did I find out that one of the congregants at my synagogue was Leo Frank.
sentences.zh: 直到我研究那本关于这一切的书时，我才发现我所在会堂的一名会众竟然是利奥·弗兰克。

sentences.en: I did not know in all of my bar mitzvah work and all of my Sunday schools and all of my confirmation, no one ever said, hey, one of the most famous Jews in
sentences.zh: 在我所有的受戒礼准备、主日学校和坚信礼学习中，我根本不知道，从来没有人说过，嘿，美国历史上最著名的犹太人之一

sentences.en: the history of America went here and he was lynched.
sentences.zh: 曾在这里做礼拜，而且他被私刑处死了。

sentences.en: I don't know that backstory.
sentences.zh: 我不知道那个背景故事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, Leo Frank was accused unjustly of having murdered a 13-year-old girl.
sentences.zh: 利奥·弗兰克被不公正地指控谋杀了一名13岁的女孩。

sentences.en: And during a vicious trial, the Southerners around Atlanta whipped up an anti-Semitic frenzy.
sentences.zh: 在一场恶毒的审判中，亚特兰大周围的南方人煽动起了一场反犹太主义的狂热。

sentences.en: He was initially convicted and sentenced to death, but the governor of Georgia at the time realized that a great miscarriage of justice had been done.
sentences.zh: 他最初被判有罪并被判处死刑，但当时的佐治亚州州长意识到这是一起巨大的司法不公。

sentences.en: He commuted his sentence to life in prison.
sentences.zh: 他将他的刑期减为终身监禁。

sentences.en: And then the good citizens of Atlanta went out to the Milledgeville State Penitentiary outside of Atlanta, hauled Leo
sentences.zh: 然后，亚特兰大的好市民们跑到亚特兰大郊外的米利奇维尔州立监狱，把利奥·

sentences.en: Frank out and lynched him.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克拖出来并对他实施了私刑。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It was a moment for American Jewry and I was not told about it growing up in this congregation, which tells you something about American Jewry's desire to put the past into the
sentences.zh: 这对美国犹太人来说是一个重要的时刻，而我在这个会众中长大时却从未被告知过，这说明了美国犹太人想要把过去留在

sentences.en: paSt. It was always a European affair.
sentences.zh: 过去。这总是一件欧洲人的事。

sentences.en: It was something that we had escaped.
sentences.zh: 这是我们已经逃离的东西。

sentences.en: It feels, Jonathan, like your surprise sort of mirrors our collective surprise over the past two years, that anti-Semitism had felt like an un-American problem.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，感觉你的惊讶似乎反映了我们过去两年来共同的惊讶，即反犹太主义曾被认为是一个非美国的问题。

sentences.en: And suddenly it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，它不再是了。

sentences.en: Once you saw in your own inbox and in your Twitter feed and your voicemail, I wonder where else did you begin to see it?
sentences.zh: 一旦你在自己的收件箱、推特动态和语音留言中看到了它，我想知道你还在哪里开始看到它？

sentences.en: You know, you get your antenna up and suddenly as the 2016 presidential campaign really kicked into gear, I started seeing it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你竖起天线，突然间随着2016年总统竞选真正进入高潮，我开始到处看到它。

sentences.en: Are you familiar with this meme called Pepe the Frog?
sentences.zh: 你熟悉这个叫“佩佩蛙”的表情包吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If you're those who don't, here's a picture.
sentences.zh: 如果你不熟悉，这是一张图片。

sentences.en: Here's Pepe the Frog, okay?
sentences.zh: 这就是佩佩蛙，好吗？

sentences.en: And one of the people who caught on to the sort of Pepe rage was Donald Trump Jr., who had a thing for retweeting a lot of neo-Nazis, interestingly enough, on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 而那些赶上这种“佩佩狂热”的人之一就是小唐纳德·特朗普，有趣的是，他在推特上非常喜欢转发许多新纳粹分子的内容。

sentences.en: He posted this on September 10th and there's Pepe right in the middle.
sentences.zh: 他在9月10日发布了这张图，佩佩就在正中间。

sentences.en: The show Solidarity with the Alt-Right.
sentences.zh: 展示了与另类右翼的团结。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: With white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 与白人至上主义的团结。

sentences.en: We have gone from dog whistles to full-on barking.
sentences.zh: 我们已经从狗哨变成了彻头彻尾的狂吠。

sentences.en: And because I knew it, I could see things out there in the campaign that other people would just go right by.
sentences.zh: 因为我了解它，所以我能在竞选中看到其他人会直接忽略的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, for instance, there was a moment where...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，例如，有那么一刻……

sentences.en: Donald Trump is facing backlash over this tweet that included the star of David.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普因这条包含大卫之星的推文而面临强烈反对。

sentences.en: The tweet shows the Jewish symbol over images of Hillary Clinton and dollar bills.
sentences.zh: 推文显示了犹太符号覆盖在希拉里·克林顿和美元钞票的图像上。

sentences.en: The message over the star says, most corrupt candidate ever.
sentences.zh: 星星上的文字写着：史上最腐败的候选人。

sentences.en: A lot of people said, wait a minute, that's a Jewish star.
sentences.zh: 很多人说，等一下，那是犹太星。

sentences.en: This must be an anti-Semitic reference.
sentences.zh: 这一定是一个反犹太主义的指涉。

sentences.en: Megan, the debate boils down to whether or not you think a six-sided star looks more like a star of David or a sheriff's badge.
sentences.zh: 梅根，争论归结为你是认为六角星看起来更像大卫之星还是警长徽章。

sentences.en: And they said, oh no, don't be silly.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦不，别傻了。

sentences.en: That's a sheriff's star.
sentences.zh: 那是警长星。

sentences.en: But because I was trolling around looking at the images on these Alt-Right websites, I knew exactly where they had gotten that.
sentences.zh: 但因为我一直在这些另类右翼网站上浏览图片，我非常清楚他们是从哪里弄来的。

sentences.en: It wasn't some innocent thing.
sentences.zh: 那不是什么无辜的东西。

sentences.en: They didn't stumble into it.
sentences.zh: 他们不是偶然碰到的。

sentences.en: They went looking for that image and somehow thought that that was a good thing to send out.
sentences.zh: 他们是专门去寻找那张图片的，并且不知何故认为把它发出来是一件好事。

sentences.en: And then the final campaign that candidate Trump ran, his closing statement for the 2016 presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 然后是特朗普候选人进行的最后一场竞选活动，他2016年总统竞选的结束语。

sentences.en: Our movement is about replacing a failed and corrupt political establishment with a
sentences.zh: 我们的运动旨在用一个由你们，即美国人民，控制的新政府来取代一个失败且腐败的政治建制派，

sentences.en: new government controlled by you, the American people, was this dark, dark ad that spoke of global special interests coming after America.
sentences.zh: 这是一个黑暗、阴沉的广告，讲述了全球特殊利益集团正在追捕美国。

sentences.en: For those who control the levers of power in Washington and for the global special interest, they partner with these people that don't have your good in mind.
sentences.zh: 对于那些控制华盛顿权力杠杆的人和全球特殊利益集团来说，他们与那些不为你们着想的人勾结在一起。

sentences.en: And as they ran these words, global special interests, you saw the Jewish faces of Janet Yellen,
sentences.zh: 当他们播放这些词汇“全球特殊利益集团”时，你看到了珍妮特·耶伦的犹太面孔，

sentences.en: the Federal Reserve chairman, of Lloyd Blankfein, the chairman of Goldman Sachs, and of George Soros,
sentences.zh: 美联储主席，高盛董事长劳埃德·布兰克费恩，以及乔治·索罗斯，

sentences.en: the Jewish philanthropiSt. Three Jewish images coming on top of those words, global special interests.
sentences.zh: 这位犹太慈善家。三个犹太人的形象出现在这些词汇之上，全球特殊利益集团。

sentences.en: It was just hard to mistake.
sentences.zh: 这简直让人无法误解。

sentences.en: And we will take back this country for you and we will make America great again.
sentences.zh: 我们将为你们夺回这个国家，我们将让美国再次伟大。

sentences.en: I'm Donald Trump and I approve this message.
sentences.zh: 我是唐纳德·特朗普，我批准这条信息。

sentences.en: But I guess there's still kind of a plausible
sentences.zh: 但我猜对于这样的事情，仍然存在某种貌似合理的

sentences.en: deniability, perhaps, to something like that.
sentences.zh: 推诿空间，也许吧。

sentences.en: And the Trump campaign, whenever they were called on it by reporters, always said, you're seeing things that aren't there.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普竞选团队，每当被记者质问时，总是说，你看到了不存在的东西。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And remember, the plausible deniability always came from the talisman that is Ivanka Trump.
sentences.zh: 记住，这种貌似合理的推诿总是来自伊万卡·特朗普这个护身符。

sentences.en: Do you think the president dislikes his daughter?
sentences.zh: 你认为总统不喜欢他的女儿吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 所以你认为总统不喜欢犹太人，并且对犹太人有偏见？

sentences.zh: 你对美国总统有这种看法？

sentences.en: You bet.

sentences.en: And do you know why?

sentences.zh: 你怎么敢指责他反犹太主义？

sentences.en: How do we understand
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解

sentences.en: what you're describing as kind of unmistakable appeals to anti-Semitism in an ad like this being present in the campaign?
sentences.zh: 你所描述的那些在竞选广告中出现的、对反犹太主义的明确诉求？

sentences.en: I think Donald Trump had a very hard time turning his back on his most ardent supporters.
sentences.zh: 我认为唐纳德·特朗普很难背弃他最狂热的支持者。

sentences.en: He and his campaign understood that they had really riled up the far right, the alt-right, and that included racists, that included anti-Semites.
sentences.zh: 他和他的竞选团队明白，他们确实激怒了极右翼、另类右翼，其中也包括种族主义者和反犹太主义者。

sentences.en: I'm not going to accuse him of racism or anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 我不会指责他有种族主义或反犹太主义倾向。

sentences.en: But I will say that when confronted with the darker sides of his supporters, he was always very reluctant to denounce them, to push them away.
sentences.zh: 但我会说，当面对其支持者阴暗的一面时，他总是非常不愿谴责他们，不愿将他们推开。

sentences.en: And that in your mind is just purely about an electoral calculation by the president and by those around him?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这纯粹是总统及其身边人的一种选举算计吗？

sentences.en: In my mind, I do not think that Donald Trump feels like he can waste or lose a single vote.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我不认为唐纳德·特朗普觉得他能浪费或失去任何一张选票。

sentences.en: So for me, Jonathan, as someone who did not have the kind of awakening that you did because of what
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，乔纳森，作为一个没有像你那样因为在推特上发生的事情

sentences.en: happened to you on Twitter, there was talk of anti-Semitism during the campaign, but it often felt a little ambiguous.

sentences.en: And I actually remember vividly when that changed.
sentences.zh: 我实际上清楚地记得那是何时改变的。

sentences.en: It was Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 那是夏洛茨维尔事件。

sentences.en: It was a white nationalist rally that seemed like it was about race.
sentences.zh: 那是一场看起来与种族有关的白人民族主义集会。

sentences.en: But suddenly you had all these young white men marching in unison and chanting, Jews will not replace us.
sentences.zh: 但突然间，你看到所有这些年轻的白人男子齐步游行，高呼：“犹太人不会取代我们。”

sentences.en: Jews will not replace us.
sentences.zh: “犹太人不会取代我们。”

sentences.en: And I remember being truly confused by that chant.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时对这个口号感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: Like, why are white nationalists talking about Jews?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么白人民族主义者要谈论犹太人？

sentences.en: It did not make a whole lot of sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说一点也说不通。

sentences.en: It made a lot of sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很有道理。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because there is kind of a pantheon of evil in the alt-right, in this new breed of neo-Nazis.
sentences.zh: 因为在另类右翼，在这个新一代的新纳粹分子中，存在着一种邪恶的万神殿。

sentences.zh: 而在那个万神殿里，口号是“白人种族灭绝”，他们相信白人种族正在被取代、被替换、被稀释。

sentences.en: And they also believe that the white race is superior to Latinos, to blacks, to anyone who's not white, right?
sentences.zh: 他们还认为白人种族优于拉丁裔、黑人，以及任何非白人，对吧？

sentences.en: And remember, Jews in their mind are not white.
sentences.zh: 记住，在他们心目中，犹太人不是白人。

sentences.en: But they look around them and they say, well, wait a minute, if we're the superior race, how could it be that these brown-skinned and black-skinned

sentences.en: people are succeeding in white genocide, are replacing us?
sentences.zh: 正在成功地实施白人种族灭绝，正在取代我们？

sentences.en: And that's where they look for the puppet master.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们寻找幕后黑手的地方。

sentences.en: And they find the Jews.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了犹太人。

sentences.en: The Jews in the alt-right world are the ones who are orchestrating the white genocide.
sentences.zh: 在另类右翼的世界里，犹太人就是策划白人种族灭绝的人。

sentences.en: Maybe not the field troops.
sentences.zh: 也许不是前线部队。

sentences.en: The shock troops of white genocide are brown-skinned and black-skinned.
sentences.zh: 白人种族灭绝的突击部队是棕色皮肤和黑色皮肤的人。

sentences.en: But the orchestrators of white genocide are Jews.
sentences.zh: 但白人种族灭绝的策划者是犹太人。

sentences.en: That's why Jews will not replace us.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么说“犹太人不会取代我们”。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because if you look at the rhetoric right now about immigration,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为如果你看看现在关于移民的言论，

sentences.en: you go back to the 1930s and you heard the same thing about immigrants and migrants and refugees coming from Europe.
sentences.zh: 回到20世纪30年代，你也会听到关于来自欧洲的移民、迁徙者和难民的同样说法。

sentences.en: And those were Jewish refugees.
sentences.zh: 而那些是犹太难民。

sentences.en: At that time in the 1930s, Americans feared Jewish children the way they seem to fear Muslim children or Mexican children now.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代，美国人恐惧犹太儿童的方式，就像他们现在似乎恐惧穆斯林儿童或墨西哥儿童一样。

sentences.en: And when Gallup would poll people about whether they supported controls on immigration or controls on the flow of refugees,
sentences.zh: 当盖洛普民意调查询问人们是否支持控制移民或控制难民潮时，

sentences.en: they were actually talking about Jewish refugees, not Syrians, not Mexicans or Guatemalans.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上谈论的是犹太难民，而不是叙利亚人，也不是墨西哥人或危地马拉人。

sentences.en: Jews were the refugees that everyone feared in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代，犹太人是每个人都恐惧的难民。

sentences.en: We are Christian in so far as we believe in Christ's principle of love your neighbor as yourself.
sentences.zh: 我们是基督徒，因为我们相信基督“爱邻如己”的原则。

sentences.en: And with that principle, I challenge every Jew in this nation to tell me that he does not believe in it.
sentences.zh: 秉持这一原则，我挑战这个国家的每一位犹太人，告诉我不相信它。

sentences.en: So what's the connection?
sentences.zh: 那么这有什么联系呢？

sentences.en: Why are Jews now seen as the puppeteers of Syrians, Mexicans, etc.?
sentences.zh: 为什么犹太人现在被视为叙利亚人、墨西哥人等的幕后操纵者？

sentences.en: Well, you know, one of the central tenets of Judaism is remember the stranger for you were a stranger in in the land of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，犹太教的核心信条之一是“记住陌生人，因为你们在埃及地也曾作过寄居的”。

sentences.en: It is actually part of the religion to welcome strangers, to welcome immigrants, to welcome refugees.
sentences.zh: 欢迎陌生人、欢迎移民、欢迎难民，这实际上是宗教的一部分。

sentences.en: And actually, American Jews really created the concept of repairing the world to
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国犹太人确实创造了“修复世界”的概念，即

sentences.zh: “修补世界”（Tikkun Olam）。

sentences.en: And this kind of welcoming response to the stranger extended in the 1950s to African Americans who were then stirring the civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 这种对陌生人的欢迎态度在20世纪50年代延伸到了当时正在掀起民权运动的非裔美国人身上。

sentences.en: I was the rabbi of the Jewish community in Berlin under the Hitler regime.

sentences.zh: 我一生中学到的最重要的事情是，偏执

sentences.en: and hatred are not the most urgent probleMs. The most urgent, the most disgraceful, the most shameful, and the most tragic problem is silence.

sentences.zh: 民权运动是犹太人和黑人结盟的一个开创性时刻。

sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金在拉比中拥有巨大的盟友，特别是在南方。

sentences.en: It must not remain silent, not merely black America, but all of America.
sentences.zh: 它绝不能保持沉默，不仅是黑人美国，而是整个美国。

sentences.en: It must speak up and act from the president down to the humblest of us.
sentences.zh: 从总统到我们中最卑微的人，都必须大声疾呼并采取行动。

sentences.en: And not for the sake of the Negro, not for the sake of the black community, but for the sake of the image, the dream, the idea, and the aspiration of America itself.
sentences.zh: 不是为了黑人，不是为了黑人社区，而是为了美国本身的形象、梦想、理念和抱负。

sentences.en: And yeah, that has tremendous resonance to Jews and to fighters and civil rights.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对犹太人和民权斗士来说有着巨大的共鸣。

sentences.en: And it also has tremendous resonance for the alt-right who always see Jews somewhere in the background orchestrating their demise.
sentences.zh: 这对另类右翼也有巨大的共鸣，他们总是认为犹太人在幕后策划他们的灭亡。

sentences.en: What's kind of complicated about this discussion is that I was so prepared to have you tell me that all these tropes you heard about were factually false.
sentences.zh: 这场讨论之所以复杂，是因为我本已准备好让你告诉我，你听到的所有这些比喻在事实上都是错误的。

sentences.en: But what's really tricky about this conversation and hard to grapple with is that Jews in America have done the things by welcoming
sentences.zh: 但这场对话真正棘手且难以应对的是，美国犹太人通过欢迎

sentences.en: outsiders that they're being accused of doing by these white nationalists in ways that completely defy all the simple hate.
sentences.zh: 局外人所做的事情，正是这些白人民族主义者指责他们所做的事情，这完全违背了所有简单的仇恨逻辑。

sentences.en: But what white nationalists believe is that these things you're describing are being done not out of altruism, not out of a kind of spirit of generosity, but to
sentences.zh: 但白人民族主义者认为，你所描述的这些事情并非出于利他主义，并非出于一种慷慨的精神，而是为了

sentences.en: undermine white people.
sentences.zh: 破坏白人。

sentences.en: They see it as something being taken away rather than something being given.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是在被剥夺，而不是在被给予。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It all fits into the alt-right world of white genocide.
sentences.zh: 这一切都符合另类右翼的“白人种族灭绝”世界观。

sentences.en: So from everything that you're saying, it would stand to reason that anti-Semitism would flare up whenever nationalism is on the rise in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以根据你所说的一切，可以推断出每当美国民族主义抬头时，反犹太主义就会爆发。

sentences.en: Or internationally.
sentences.zh: 或者在国际上也是如此。

sentences.en: And frankly, it is my view, and this is a controversial view, that when borders are blurred, when distinctions actually are diminished, Jews tend to flourish.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我的观点是——这是一个有争议的观点——当边界模糊，当区别实际上减少时，犹太人往往会繁荣。

sentences.en: But when the drawbridge is raised, when borders are more clearly defined, when people are defining sharply what it means to be an American, or a Frenchman, or a Briton,
sentences.zh: 但当吊桥升起，当边界被更清晰地定义，当人们尖锐地定义什么是美国人、法国人或英国人时，

sentences.en: those are bad times for Jews.
sentences.zh: 对犹太人来说就是糟糕的时期。

sentences.en: Because as nationalism rises, and as these ethnic and national distinctions are sharpened, the Jews tend to be left out of that definition.
sentences.zh: 因为随着民族主义的兴起，随着这些种族和民族的区别变得尖锐，犹太人往往被排除在这个定义之外。

sentences.en: They tend to be isolated, and eventually they tend to be persecuted.
sentences.zh: 他们往往被孤立，最终往往受到迫害。

sentences.en: of Trump supporters and he undermines the support that Donald Trump should have from American Jews.

sentences.en: Our message to the organizers and participants of this caravan is simple.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
